items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Bodaly opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.
Councillor Bodaly offered further reflections on land acknowledgements and the lands he grew up on in Sudbury.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Bodaly provided Council with moments of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

On International Women’s Day, we celebrate the progress we’ve made toward gender equality while recognizing the important work that lies ahead. The City of Waterloo remains dedicated to creating an equitable and inclusive community that is free from discrimination and where women, girls and gender-diverse individuals can thrive.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Roe attended the Waterloo Pentecostal Assembly’s Dinner on King, formerly called Feeding Frenzi, Last Thursday, March 5. They feed up to 250 students on Thursdays. She had a great time speaking to the students and hearing about their positive experiences in Waterloo.

Councillor Wright thanked the Waterloo Region Small Business Centre, the Uptown Waterloo BIA, and the Women in Communications and Technology group. They hosted a Market and Panel Discussion event for International Women’s Day at CIGI. It was really well attended and the panel discussion was well presented.

motions.text: 1. That the Council (“Council”) of The Corporation of the City of Waterloo (the “City”), as approving authority under the Expropriations Act, R.S.O., 1990, c. E26 (the “Expropriations Act”), consider the Report dated December 24, 2025 issued by the Ontario Land Tribunal (“Tribunal”) associated with a Hearing of Necessity that was heard under Section 7 of the Expropriations Act on December 13, 2024 in connection with the expropriation referred to below and identified as OLT Case No: OLT-24-000819 attached as Schedule A to this Staff Report. 2. That Council approve the expropriation of all right, title and interest in and to the land legally described as: PT MILL SQUARE AND PART OF ERB STREET PL 385 CITY OF WATERLOO being Part of PIN 22411-0263 (LT) designated as Parts 1 and 2 on the draft Reference Plan prepared by James M. Laws of Van Harten Surveying Inc., Project No. 29240-21 dated March 13, 2024 and bearing revision date March 20, 2024 attached as Schedule “B” to this Staff Report (the “Lands”) for the municipal purpose(s) of the advancement of a master plan for the short-term, medium-term and long-term use and development of lands at and in the vicinity of PIN 22411-0263, in the City of Waterloo in furtherance of the economic and social well- being and parking rationalization of the City, implementation of community improvement objectives, realization of the Uptown Public Realm Strategy (March 19, 2019), promotion of good land use planning principles and Official Plan policies, implementation of Provincial Policy Statement policies, facilitation of required housing and considerations under Royal Assent of Bill 23 (More Homes Built Faster Act), together with completion of any future acquisitions and/or dispositions of land including transactions involving any or all of the Lands in furtherance of the foregoing municipal purposes and objectives. 3. That Council authorize the Mayor and City Clerk or their designates to execute the appropriate Certificate of Approval in a form satisfactory to the City Solicitor. 4. That Council authorize the City to take all necessary steps to complete the expropriation and comply with the Expropriations Act including, but not limited to: a. cause the decision and written reasons for the approval to expropriate to be executed by the City Clerk and be served upon all necessary parties insubstantial conformity with Schedule D to this Staff Report; b. prepare and register in the proper land registry office a Certificate of Approval, as necessary; c. prepare and register in the proper land registry office a Plan of Expropriation; and d. execute and serve Notices of Expropriation, Notices of Election and Notices of Possession, as may be required. 5. That Council authorize the City Solicitor, and/or designate, to execute applicable documents and notices associated with the expropriation including, without limitation: a. Notices of Expropriation; b. Notices of Possession; c. Section 25 Offers of Compensation (and to obtain an appraisal report pursuant to and in accordance with Section 25 of the Expropriations Act in connection therewith); and d. Applications or any other legal materials with respect to securing possession of the Lands under and pursuant to Section 39 of the Expropriations Act; 6. That Council authorize the City to serve Offers of Compensation pursuant to and under Section 25 of the Expropriations Act in connection with the expropriation. 7. That Council Authorize the City to pay compensation upon acceptance of any Offer of Compensation. 8. That Council authorize the City Solicitor to discontinue expropriation proceedings or any part thereof, in respect of the above described lands, or any part thereof should it be determined in the City Solicitor’s opinion that the expropriation is no longer necessary by reason of the completion of negotiated transactions that dispense with the need for expropriation or for any other purpose or reason in the advancement of the interests of the City. 9. That Council authorize the City Solicitor, and/or designate, to do all other things required in connection with the expropriation and/or arising from the recommendations herein. 10. That the necessary by-law(s) related to the recommendations herein be enacted.

3. That Council authorize the Mayor and City Clerk or their designates to execute the appropriate Certificate of Approval in a form satisfactory to the City Solicitor.

4. That Council authorize the City to take all necessary steps to complete the expropriation and comply with the Expropriations Act including, but not limited to: a. cause the decision and written reasons for the approval to expropriate to be executed by the City Clerk and be served upon all necessary parties insubstantial conformity with Schedule D to this Staff Report; b. prepare and register in the proper land registry office a Certificate of Approval, as necessary; c. prepare and register in the proper land registry office a Plan of Expropriation; and d. execute and serve Notices of Expropriation, Notices of Election and Notices of Possession, as may be required.

5. That Council authorize the City Solicitor, and/or designate, to execute applicable documents and notices associated with the expropriation including, without limitation: a. Notices of Expropriation; b. Notices of Possession; c. Section 25 Offers of Compensation (and to obtain an appraisal report pursuant to and in accordance with Section 25 of the Expropriations Act in connection therewith); and d. Applications or any other legal materials with respect to securing possession of the Lands under and pursuant to Section 39 of the Expropriations Act;

6. That Council authorize the City to serve Offers of Compensation pursuant to and under Section 25 of the Expropriations Act in connection with the expropriation.

7. That Council Authorize the City to pay compensation upon acceptance of any Offer of Compensation.

8. That Council authorize the City Solicitor to discontinue expropriation proceedings or any part thereof, in respect of the above described lands, or any part thereof should it be determined in the City Solicitor’s opinion that the expropriation is no longer necessary by reason of the completion of negotiated transactions that dispense with the need for expropriation or for any other purpose or reason in the advancement of the interests of the City.

9. That Council authorize the City Solicitor, and/or designate, to do all other things required in connection with the expropriation and/or arising from the recommendations herein.

10. That the necessary by-law(s) related to the recommendations herein be enacted.
